from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Complex signals are chords of pure sine notes.", "A spectrum analyzer reveals these individual frequencies.", "Fourier series is the sheet music of waves."]
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Musical Analogy", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display musical score on screen, highlight individual notes in #FFD700.
        note_group = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE),
            Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE),
            Circle(radius=0.2, color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT)
        self.place_at_grid(note_group, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(note_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(note_group.animate.set_color("#FFD700"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Introduce harmony staff, show overlapping waves in #00FFFF.
        wave_group = VGroup(
            Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1, 1, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.3),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x * 5), color="#00FFFF"),
            FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(x * 10), color="#00FFFF")
        )
        self.place_at_grid(wave_group, 'D2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(wave_group))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade out notes, bring in vector representation in #FFFFFF.
        self.play(FadeOut(note_group))
        vector = Arrow(ORIGIN, UP*1, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(vector, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(GrowArrow(vector))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Sine and cosine functions are perfectly orthogonal.",
            "Like spatial axes, they don't interfere.",
            "This orthogonality isolates specific signal components."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Refresher: Orthogonality", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw two perpendicular vectors labeled 'a' and 'b' in #FF4500
        vec_a = Vector([0, 1.5], color="#FF4500")
        vec_b = Vector([1.5, 0], color="#FF4500")
        label_a = MathTex(r"\vec{a}", color="#FF4500").next_to(vec_a.get_end(), UP)
        label_b = MathTex(r"\vec{b}", color="#FF4500").next_to(vec_b.get_end(), RIGHT)
        
        axes_group = VGroup(vec_a, vec_b, label_a, label_b)
        self.place_in_area(axes_group, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(vec_a), Create(vec_b), Write(label_a), Write(label_b))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show dot product calculation equaling zero in #00FF00
        dot_product = MathTex(r"\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 0", color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_product, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(dot_product))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate projection of one vector onto another in #FFFF00
        # For simplicity, represent projection as a dashed line/arc
        proj_line = DashedLine(vec_a.get_end(), vec_b.get_start(), color="#FFFF00")
        proj_label = MathTex(r"\text{proj}", color="#FFFF00", font_size=24).next_to(proj_line, DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(proj_line), Write(proj_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The Fourier series builds waves from components.",
            "The constant a0 sets the average height.",
            "Coefficients an and bn define harmonic volume.",
            "Adding sine waves approximates complex shapes.",
            "Summing more harmonics creates a perfect square."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Formula: Building Blocks", lecture_lines)
        
        # Formula setup
        formula = MathTex(
            "f(t) = \\frac{a_0}{2} + \\sum_{n=1}^{\\infty} [a_n \\cos(n\\omega t) + b_n \\sin(n\\omega t)]",
            font_size=36
        )
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF1493"))
        self.play(Indicate(formula[0][5:9], color="#FF1493"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(formula[0][16:21], color="#00BFFF"), Indicate(formula[0][24:29], color="#00BFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#ADFF2F"))
        # Visualization of sine sum (simple conceptual representation)
        sine = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x), x_range=[-PI, PI])
        self.place_at_grid(sine, "D3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(sine))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        square = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1 if x > 0 else -1, x_range=[-PI, PI])
        self.place_at_grid(square, "E3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Transform(sine, square))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Calculating Coefficients: The Detective Work", [
            "We extract coefficients using integral filtering.",
            "The basis function acts as a sieve.",
            "This process isolates pure sine wave amplitudes."
        ])

        # Setup Axes and Signal
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 7, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        
        signal = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x) + 0.5 * np.cos(2*x), x_range=[0, 2*PI], color="#FF4500")
        basis = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x), x_range=[0, 2*PI], color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(signal))
        self.play(Create(basis.set_color("#FF4500")))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        area = axes.get_area(signal, x_range=[0, 2*PI], color="#00FFFF", opacity=0.3)
        self.play(Create(area))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        coeff_text = MathTex("a_n = \\frac{1}{\\pi} \\int f(x) \\sin(nx) dx").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(coeff_text, "A1")
        self.play(Write(coeff_text))
        
        val = DecimalNumber(0.75, num_decimal_places=2, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(val, "C3")
        self.play(FadeIn(val))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Real-World Application", 
                         ["Fourier series maps time signals to frequencies.", 
                          "This data enables modern signal compression.", 
                          "Technology discards irrelevant data to optimize storage."])
        
        self.lecture.set_opacity(1)

        # Assets
        # 1. Complex Signal / Frequency Spectrum
        time_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        signal = time_axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * PI * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(4 * PI * x), color="#FFD700")
        
        freq_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        spectrum = VGroup(
            Line(freq_axes.c2p(1,0), freq_axes.c2p(1,1), color="#FFD700"),
            Line(freq_axes.c2p(2,0), freq_axes.c2p(2,0.5), color="#FFD700")
        )
        
        # 2. Audio Equalizer
        eq = VGroup(*[Rectangle(height=np.random.rand()*1.5, width=0.3, fill_opacity=0.8, color="#00FF00") for _ in range(5)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        # 3. Clean Reconstructed Signal
        recon_signal = time_axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * PI * x), color="#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(time_axes, signal), "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(freq_axes, spectrum), "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(eq, "D3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(recon_signal, "F3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Pure Fourier Series: Decoding the Language of Waves

sections.title: The Hook: The Musical Analogy
sections.content: Introduce the concept that any complex periodic signal is just a chord made of pure sine and cosine notes. Use a visual of a 'Spectrum Analyzer' where a messy wave transforms into individual, neat, vertical bars (frequencies).
sections.example: Imagine a musician playing a complex chord on a piano; the Fourier Series is the sheet music that tells us exactly which individual keys (sines/cosines) were pressed to create that specific sound.

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: Orthogonality
sections.content: Briefly explain that sine and cosine functions are 'orthogonal'—like the x, y, and z axes in space. This property allows us to isolate specific components of a wave without them interfering with each other.
sections.example: Visualizing two perpendicular vectors in 3D space: projecting a vector onto the X-axis ignores the Y and Z components, just as integration isolates a single frequency from a complex signal.

sections.title: The Mathematical Formula: Building Blocks
sections.content: Present the Fourier Series equation: f(t) = a0/2 + Σ[an cos(nωt) + bn sin(nωt)]. Break down the components visually: the constant 'a0' as the average height, and 'an/bn' as the 'volume' (amplitude) of each harmonic.
sections.example: An animation showing a square wave being built by adding together sine waves of increasing frequency. First, one bump, then three, then ten—until it looks like a perfect square.

sections.title: Calculating Coefficients: The Detective Work
sections.content: Explain how we extract the 'an' and 'bn' coefficients using the integral of the function multiplied by the basis function (sin/cos). This is the 'filtering' process.
sections.example: A visual 'Sieve' metaphor: passing the complex signal through a filter that only lets through a specific frequency, leaving behind a pure sine wave whose amplitude equals the coefficient.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize that the Fourier Series turns time-domain signals into frequency-domain data. Connect this to modern technology.
sections.example: Show how a smartphone compresses a voice recording by identifying the dominant frequencies and discarding the tiny, irrelevant ones, much like a chef removing seeds to make a smooth purée.
